platform.name: ORBIT
platform.tagline: AI-assisted dental radiology education — curriculum console

modules.title: Image Quality and Error Correction
modules.description: Develop the ability to identify radiographic errors, understand their causes, and apply corrective techniques to produce diagnostic-quality images.

objectives.text: Accurately classify radiographs as diagnostic or non-diagnostic with ≥90% accuracy
Identify common radiographic errors (e.g., cone cut, overlap, elongation, foreshortening, motion artifact, exposure errors) with ≥ 90% accuracy
Determine the most likely cause of radiographic errors, including positioning, angulation, receptor placement, and exposure technique, in ≥90% of cases
Select the appropriate corrective action needed to produce a diagnostic-quality image in ≥90% of cases
Differentiate errors requiring retake from acceptable diagnostic variation in ≥90% of cases
Explain how specific image quality errors impact diagnostic interpretation and clinical decision-making in ≥90% of responses

modules.title: Radiographic Mounting
modules.description: Build skills to correctly orient and mount intraoral radiographs using standard conventions and anatomical cues

objectives.text: Correctly orient intraoral radiographs (maxillary vs mandibular, right vs left) with ≥90% accuracy
Assemble bitewing and full-mouth radiographic series (FMX) using standard mounting conventions with ≥90% accuracy
Identify anatomical landmarks used to determine radiographic orientation in ≥90% of cases
Differentiate correctly mounted from incorrectly mounted radiographs with ≥90% accuracy
Apply spatial reasoning to localize radiographic structures within the oral cavity in ≥90% of cases
Correct mounting and orientation errors using anatomical and positional cues in ≥90% of exercises

modules.title: Tooth Identification and Localization
modules.description: Establish fluency in identifying and localizing teeth across radiographic views using morphology, position

objectives.text: Correctly identify teeth on bitewing and periapical radiographs using the Universal numbering system with ≥90% accuracy
Correctly determine whether a radiograph shows the right or left side of the mouth with ≥90% accuracy
Correctly determine whether a radiograph is maxillary or mandibular with ≥85% accuracy
Use tooth shape, root structure, and position within the arch to distinguish between similar teeth on radiographs with ≥80% accuracy
Correctly identify adjacent teeth and tooth relationships on radiographs with ≥90% accuracy
Identify missing, restored, impacted, or malpositioned teeth on radiographs with ≥90% accuracy

modules.title: Normal Anatomy vs Pathology
modules.description: Train learners to differentiate normal anatomical structures and radiographic artifacts from pathology through pattern recognition and visual discrimination.

objectives.text: Correctly classify radiographic findings as normal anatomy, radiographic artifact, or pathology with ≥90% accuracy
Identify common normal anatomical structures on radiographs (e.g., mental foramen, maxillary sinus, nutrient canals) with ≥90% accuracy
Differentiate common radiographic artifacts and normal anatomical variations from caries or periapical pathology in ≥90% of cases
Correctly identify false-positive trap cases (e.g., cervical burnout, overlapping contacts, mental foramen) with ≥90% accuracy
Use radiographic features such as shape, border definition, location, and symmetry to justify whether a finding is normal or pathologic in ≥90% of responses
Avoid overdiagnosing normal anatomical structures or artifacts as pathology in ≥90% of cases
Demonstrate improved accuracy in distinguishing normal anatomy from pathology after AI dialogue or annotation review in ≥15% of applicable cases

cases.name: Nutrient Canal Mimic
cases.notes: Linear radiolucency mistaken for fracture or lesion

cases.name: Maxillary Sinus Superimposition
cases.notes: Sinus floor mistaken for pathology near molar roots

modules.title: Radiographic Interpretation & AI Comparison
modules.description: Apply structured diagnostic reasoning to identify pathology, then compare, refine, and justify interpretations through AI-assisted dialogue and feedback.

objectives.text: Correctly identify common radiographic findings, including caries, bone loss, periapical lesions, and restorative defects, with ≥90% accuracy
Correctly identify the affected tooth and surface associated with a radiographic finding with ≥90% accuracy
Use radiographic evidence, including radiolucency pattern, location, border definition, and surrounding structures, to support diagnostic decisions in ≥90% of responses
Differentiate true pathology from overlapping structures, artifacts, or normal anatomy in ≥90% of cases
Compare personal diagnostic interpretations with AI-generated feedback and determine whether the AI interpretation is correct in ≥90% of cases
Appropriately accept, refine, or challenge AI-generated interpretations using radiographic evidence in ≥90% of interactions
Demonstrate improvement in diagnostic accuracy after AI dialogue or annotation review in ≥15% of applicable cases
Avoid changing a correct diagnosis to an incorrect diagnosis after AI or annotation feedback in ≥90% of applicable cases
Demonstrate improved confidence calibration by aligning confidence scores with diagnostic accuracy in ≥90% of cases

cases.name: Distal Caries vs Overlap
cases.notes: Differentiate true caries from contact overlap

cases.name: Periapical Lesion vs Mental Foramen
cases.notes: AI may incorrectly suggest periapical pathology

modules.title: Clinical Documentation and EHR Simulation
modules.description: Translate radiographic findings into accurate clinical documentation by selecting the correct tooth, surfaces, and diagnoses within a simulated EHR workflow

objectives.text: Correctly select the affected tooth on a digital odontogram based on radiographic findings with ≥90% accuracy
Correctly identify and chart the affected tooth surfaces (M, D, O, B, L) with 90% accuracy
Accurately assign radiographic findings or diagnoses within the simulated EHR workflow in ≥85% of cases
Differentiate between findings that require treatment, monitoring, or no intervention in ≥80% of cases
Use patient history, symptoms, and radiographic findings together to support charting and treatment decisions in ≥90% of cases
Complete the correct clinical workflow sequence (review radiograph → interpret findings → chart diagnosis) in ≥90% of exercises
Avoid documentation errors involving incorrect tooth selection, wrong surface selection, or incorrect diagnosis assignment in ≥85% of cases
Revise charting decisions appropriately after AI dialogue or annotation review in ≥90% of applicable cases
Demonstrate improved efficiency in completing radiographic charting tasks over repeated cases while maintaining diagnostic accuracy in ≥80% of exercises

modules.title: Panoramic View
modules.description: Interpreting panoramic radiographs, including recognition of anatomy, distortions, artifacts, and diagnostic limitations.

objectives.text: Correctly identify major anatomical structures on panoramic radiographs with ≥90% accuracy
Correctly determine whether panoramic findings represent normal anatomy, artifact, distortion, or pathology in ≥80% of cases
Identify common panoramic imaging errors and distortions (e.g., ghost images, positioning errors, magnification, blurring) with ≥90% accuracy
Differentiate true pathology from panoramic artifacts or superimposed structures in ≥90% of cases
Recognize when panoramic imaging is appropriate or insufficient for diagnostic evaluation in ≥80% of scenarios
Correctly localize radiographic findings to the appropriate region of the jaws on panoramic images with ≥90% accuracy
Use panoramic radiographic features, including symmetry, location, and border definition, to support interpretation decisions in ≥90% of responses
Compare personal interpretations with AI-generated feedback and appropriately accept, refine, or challenge AI-supported findings in ≥90% of applicable cases
Demonstrate improved accuracy in identifying panoramic artifacts and distortions after AI dialogue or annotation review in ≥15% of applicable cases

modules.title: Advanced Cases & Clinical Decision Making
modules.description: Integrate radiographic interpretation, clinical context, AI interaction, and decision-making in complex, ambiguous cases requiring prioritization and judgment

objectives.text: Correctly identify multiple radiographic findings within a single case with ≥90% accuracy
Correctly determine which radiographic finding is the highest clinical priority in ≥90% of cases
Differentiate findings that require treatment, monitoring, referral, or no intervention in ≥90% of cases
Use radiographic evidence, patient history, symptoms, and risk factors together to support clinical decision-making in ≥90% of responses
Correctly distinguish clinically significant pathology from incidental findings, normal anatomy, or radiographic artifacts in ≥90% of cases
Appropriately accept, refine, or challenge AI-generated interpretations and treatment recommendations using radiographic evidence in ≥90% of interactions
Avoid changing a correct diagnosis or management decision to an incorrect one after AI or annotation feedback in ≥90% of applicable cases
Demonstrate improvement in diagnostic accuracy and management decisions after AI dialogue or annotation review in ≥15% of applicable cases
Provide evidence-based justification for treatment, monitoring, or referral decisions in ≥90% of responses
Demonstrate improved efficiency in evaluating complex multi-finding cases while maintaining diagnostic accuracy in ≥90% of exercises

M1-05.feedback: Reducing movement improves image clarity and diagnostic quality.

M1-06.prompt: Is this radiograph diagnostic or non-diagnostic?

M1-06.prompt: What most likely caused this error?
M1-06.feedback: Insufficient exposure results in a light image with reduced diagnostic value.

M1-06.prompt: What adjustment would best correct this issue?

M1-07.prompt: Is this radiograph diagnostic or non-diagnostic?

M1-07.prompt: What most likely caused this error?
M1-07.feedback: Excessive exposure results in a dark image and loss of detail.

M1-07.prompt: What adjustment would best correct this issue?
M1-07.feedback: Reducing exposure improves image quality and diagnostic value.

M1-08.feedback: The image receptor was reversed during exposure.
